name: Issyk-Ata Gorge
near: The resort settlement of Ysyk-Ata / Karagai-Bulak village (the sanatorium’s address on 2GIS); lower down the valley — the villages in the Ivanovka direction. The district center is the town of Kant.
elev: The resort is at about 1,775 m (sxodim); the peaks at the head of the gorge reach ~3,200 m (per TripAdvisor reviews), Mount Botvei/Batyi is ~3,800 m (sxodim; not confirmed by a second source).
short: Issyk-Ata is a gorge in the Kyrgyz Ala-Too ~60–75 km from Bishkek with one of the oldest resorts in the region: hot hydrogen sulfide springs (~54 °C), waterfalls and an ancient image of the Buddha on a rock.
desc: The Issyk-Ata (Ysyk-Ata) Gorge lies on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too in the Ysyk-Ata District. The main point is the Yssyk-Ata resort-sanatorium, operating since the late 19th century (sxodim: 1891, too.kg: 1895): hydrogen sulfide thermal water at 50–60 °C comes out of the ground and is cooled to ~36 °C for the pools and baths; it is used to treat the musculoskeletal system, skin and digestive tract. In the 2020s the resort was reconstructed: separate bathing areas, new buildings and A-frame cabins, an amphitheater, salt rooms, mud therapy. Above the resort there are trails to waterfalls: the nearest, “Marble” (~10 m), is ~1.5 km away, then Bala-Partak and Jary-Tash, and the lakes of the Ayak-Kol area (the largest is Orto-Kol). On a rock near the resort is an image of the Buddha with Tibetan inscriptions (dating differs between sources: the 10th century or the 12th–14th centuries) — a reminder that the gorge was one of the region’s Buddhist centers.
guide: Issyk-Ata is an ideal “mountains + thermal baths” day: in the morning climb to the waterfalls, after lunch soak in the sanatorium’s hot pool. The nearest Marble Waterfall is 1.5 km from the resort; for the far waterfalls allow 2–3 hours and take water. Be sure to find the stone with the image of the Buddha and Tibetan inscriptions — a reminder that in the Middle Ages there was a Buddhist center here. Locals tell a legend that Amir Timur himself was cured of an illness here. On weekends the resort is overcrowded — it is better to come on weekdays.
see: The hot hydrogen sulfide springs and the sanatorium’s pools; the stone with the Buddha image and Tibetan inscriptions; the Marble Waterfall (~10 m, 1.5 km from the resort), the Bala-Partak and Jary-Tash waterfalls; the Ayak-Kol lakes (Orto-Kol); coniferous forests and meadows in the upper reaches.
skip: You are looking for wilderness without people — the resort and the lower part of the gorge are crowded, with Soviet-era buildings and litter on the trails (TripAdvisor reviews). You are not interested in thermal baths — the waterfalls are more impressive at Kegety or Ala-Archa. You dislike disorganized service — 2GIS reviews complain about booking and cleaning.
diff: Easy–moderate: from the parking lot from 2.5 km and from 1 h on foot with a gain from 250 m to the nearest waterfall, 2–3 out of 5 on the hiking.kg scale; to the far waterfalls and lakes — 3+ h (TripAdvisor). Bathing in the thermal pools — no exertion, but with health restrictions (heart, blood pressure).
when: July–September is the peak trekking season (sxodim); the thermal baths work year-round and are especially popular in winter. Many cafés and hotels work only in summer (TripAdvisor).
hours: Sanatorium: 08:00–17:00 per sxodim; pools per 2GIS — Monday closed, Tuesday 12:00–21:00, Wednesday–Sunday 09:00–21:00 (07.10.2026). Tel. +996 709 833 833, WhatsApp +996 990 250 000, Instagram @sanatorii_ysyk_ata. The gorge and trails — no time restrictions.
daytime: Morning — for the climb to the waterfalls (fewer people, cooler); evening — for the thermal baths. On weekends come when the pools open.
how: From Bishkek ~58 km, 1 h 25 min by car (hiking.kg; sxodim — 77 km, too.kg — 40–50 km, depending on the starting point) via Koi-Tash/Gornaya Maevka (the upper road) or via Ivanovka (the lower road). Marshrutka (minibus) No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station to the resort (too.kg). Beyond that, to the waterfalls — on foot.
needcar: Yes, but marshrutka No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station is enough; a car or taxi is more convenient. Inside the gorge, to the waterfalls — on foot.
self: Yes: marshrutka No. 316 to the resort, pools without reservations, the trails to the nearest waterfalls are clear. For the far lakes you need an offline map.
roadtype: To the sanatorium — paved, in places of poor quality (sxodim: paved approach); to the waterfalls — trails.
traveltime: Bishkek → resort: 1 h 25 min by car (hiking.kg), about 1.5 h by marshrutka (TripAdvisor). Resort → nearest waterfall: from 2.5 km and from 1 h, gain from 250 m (hiking.kg); the Marble Waterfall — 1.5 km (too.kg).
stay: “Yssyk-Ata” sanatorium: rooms from 7,500 som a night, wellness packages with treatments and meals from 2,200 som (mir24, 2025–2026); new A-frames (2GIS reviews). Private guesthouses in the settlement — 700–2,500 som (2GIS reviews). Camping below the resort is limited, above it up the gorge it is possible (too.kg).
net: There is mobile coverage up to the resort grounds, further up the gorge — none (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
entry: According to hiking.kg, since 2025 entry to the sanatorium grounds has been paid — the amount is not published. A pool — from 100 som (too.kg), 200 som in 2GIS reviews; parking is paid (sxodim; 300 som in 2GIS reviews). The exact 2026 tariff is not confirmed.
transfer: Marshrutka No. 316 — 50 som (too.kg); taxi and excursion prices are not given in the sources (Kyrgyz Guided Tours/Silk Road Explore — on request).
bring: Swimwear, a towel and flip-flops for the thermal baths, trekking shoes and water for the waterfalls (do not drink from the river — only springs, too.kg), food with you (the cafés work mostly in summer), warm clothes for the evening (1,775 m), cash.
warn: Hot hydrogen sulfide baths are not recommended for heart disease and high blood pressure — ask the sanatorium’s doctor. Do not drink river water. The signal ends at the resort. On weekends and holidays it is overcrowded — book accommodation in advance. An entry/parking fee was introduced in 2025 — demand a receipt.
food: Cafés on the resort grounds and grocery shops (too.kg); mineral water from the springs; meals as part of the sanatorium packages (from 2,200 som). The sources name no specific well-known establishments; 2GIS reviews complain about cold food in the cafés.
reviews: 2GIS (“Yssyk-Ata” sanatorium): 4.8/5, 1,533 ratings, 234 reviews (07.10.2026); TripAdvisor “Issyk-Ata Gorge”: 4.5/5, 39 reviews. Pros: hot pools, nature, waterfalls, new A-frames. Cons: old Soviet buildings, litter on the trails, disorganized booking, rude staff, hot-water problems.
p.sum: Issyk-Ata is a convenient day trip from Bishkek: marshrutka No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station (40–50 som, roughly once an hour, about 1.5 h) goes straight to the “Ysyk-Ata” sanatorium. There are thermal pools with 54 °C spring water (per Travelbar — 200 som for adults, 100 som for children), the stone with the Buddha and trails to waterfalls: the Marble one is 1.5 km away, the nearest big one is 2.5 km with a 250 m gain. After a major renovation (opened 17.12.2024) the sanatorium belongs to the Presidential Administration. Since 2025 entry to the grounds and parking are paid, but we did not find an official tariff. On weekends there can be a real queue, and phone reservations are not always honored (Kaktus, 06.2026).

p.iti.0.title: A day from Bishkek
p.iti.0.plan: 8:00 marshrutka No. 316 from the Eastern Bus Station → 9:30 resort → 10:00–13:00 hike to the waterfall 2.5 km and back → 13:30 lunch → 14:30–16:00 thermal pool → 17:00 marshrutka back
p.iti.1.title: 2 days
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Issyk-Ata — waterfalls and pools, a night at the sanatorium or a guesthouse. Day 2: an early start to the far waterfalls and the Ayak-Kol lakes, or a move to Chunkurchak (≈1.5 h) — a bridge, horses, a night at Supara (as in the Orexca tour)
p.iti.2.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.2.plan: The Burana Tower (via Tokmok, ≈1 h), the Kegety gorge and waterfall (≈1 h east via Rot-Front), Chunkurchak and the Alamedin gorge (to the west)
p.season: July–September: the best time for hikes to the waterfalls and lakes. The thermal baths work year-round and are especially popular in winter; on weekends and holidays there are queues. Many cafés and guesthouses work only in summer. In spring and early summer ticks are possible on the trails (a general risk for the Ala-Too foothills)
p.budget.economy: ≈600–1,200 som: marshrutka 80–100 som round trip, pool 200 som, entry (if charged to pedestrians — the amount is not confirmed), lunch at a café 300–500 som
p.budget.comfort: A taxi or a car with a driver ≈2,000–4,000 som (estimate), a night at the sanatorium from 7,500 som or a package from 2,200 som; the Orexca 2-day tour $310–620/person.
p.permits: No permits are needed. Since 2025 entry to the sanatorium grounds has been paid (hiking.kg), and parking too (≈300 som per reviews); the official 2025–26 tariff is not published — demand a receipt
p.access: Good with children and older people: paved road, pools, a playground; a child’s pool ticket is 100 som. A stroller — on the sanatorium grounds, not to the waterfalls. Hot baths are contraindicated in heart disease and hypertension. Dogs: probably not allowed on the sanatorium grounds (rules not found)
